```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("Facility_Location")
    m.setParam("TimeLimit", 100)

    # Problem Data
    facilities = list(range(6))  # F0..F5
    customers = list(range(19))  # C0..C18

    # Facility coordinates (x, y)
    facility_coords = [(92, 33), (12, 70), (41, 96), (76, 36), (11, 17), (8, 51)]

    # Customer coordinates (x, y)
    customer_coords = [(85, 49), (96, 46), (60, 16), (69, 58), (49, 57), (36, 93), (77, 55), (70, 85), (77, 90), (54, 37), (65, 83), (57, 42), (29, 79), (36, 73), (75, 30), (14, 21), (60, 3), (52, 63), (38, 45)]

    facility_capacities = [320.0, 256.0, 152.0, 265.0, 259.0, 280.0]
    customer_demands = [68.0, 56.0, 42.0, 19.0, 51.0, 17.0, 55.0, 21.0, 42.0, 42.0, 22.0, 25.0, 47.0, 24.0, 60.0, 63.0, 56.0, 60.0, 28.0]
    fixed_costs = [318.0, 325.0, 208.0, 233.0, 195.0, 317.0]
    transport_rate = 0.34  # $/km/unit

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates (INDUCED COSTS)
    def euclidean_distance(coord1, coord2):
        return math.sqrt((coord1[0] - coord2[0])**2 + (coord1[1] - coord2[1])**2)

    distances = {}
    for i in facilities:
        for j in customers:
            distances[(i, j)] = euclidean_distance(facility_coords[i], customer_coords[j])

    # Decision Variables
    # Open_F{i}: Binary - whether facility i is opened
    open_facility = {}
    for i in facilities:
        open_facility[i] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Open_F{i}")

    # Ship_F{i}_C{j}: Continuous - units shipped from facility i to customer j
    ship = {}
    for i in facilities:
        for j in customers:
            ship[(i, j)] = m.addVar(lb=0.0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_F{i}_C{j}")

    # Objective: Minimize fixed costs + transport costs
    # Transport cost = distance * rate * units shipped
    obj = quicksum(fixed_costs[i] * open_facility[i] for i in facilities)
    obj += quicksum(
        distances[(i, j)] * transport_rate * ship[(i, j)]
        for i in facilities for j in customers
    )
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # Demand satisfaction constraints
    for j in customers:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(ship[(i, j)] for i in facilities) >= customer_demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_C{j}"
        )

    # Capacity constraints (can only ship if facility is open)
    for i in facilities:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(ship[(i, j)] for j in customers) <= facility_capacities[i] * open_facility[i],
            name=f"Capacity_F{i}"
        )

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Subject: Choosing which warehouses to open and how to serve customers at the lowest total cost

Team,

We’re at a decision point on our distribution network. We have six candidate warehouse locations and nineteen customer delivery points across our service region. The candidate warehouse sites are provided as map coordinates in {FACILITY_COORDINATES}, and the customer locations are provided in {CUSTOMER_COORDINATES}. Opening any warehouse carries a one-time fixed cost, listed in {FIXED_COSTS}. Moving product from warehouses to customers will incur transportation charges that scale with how far we ship and how much volume moves, at a rate of {TRANSPORT_RATE}.

A few rules shape this decision. A warehouse can only ship if we choose to open it. Each warehouse has a throughput limit we cannot exceed; those limits are in {FACILITY_CAPACITIES}. Every customer’s demand must be fully satisfied within the planning horizon; those volumes are captured in {CUSTOMER_DEMANDS}. In short, our choices are: which warehouses to open and how to allocate each customer’s orders to the open sites.

The trade-offs are straightforward. Opening more sites increases fixed costs but can cut delivery distances and reduce shipping spend. Opening fewer sites lowers fixed costs but may push volumes farther, drive up transportation costs, and create capacity pressure. Some sites may be cheaper to open but sit farther from dense demand; others may cost more to open but sit closer to multiple high-volume customers. We need to balance these effects.

Our goal is to minimize total cost—the combination of warehouse opening costs and shipping costs—while meeting all customer demand and staying within each facility’s capacity. With the data above, we will evaluate alternative networks and flows and recommend the set of sites to open and the shipment plan that delivers the lowest total cost without compromising service.
